findings.title: Labeled RSC weighting does not descend through the full unoriented stabilizer
findings.claim_checked: Arbitrary nonnegative continuous compactly supported labeled-shape weights give Stab(gamma)-invariant horoball measures.
assumptions_checked: Genus g=3, simple essential nonseparating length-1 curve
Positive trivalent ribbon graph in MRG_{2,2}(1,1), boundary cycles 14 and 10 darts
Exact realization by Luo Theorem1.2/Cor1.4, projection width coordinate checked against Mondello v4
h nonnegative continuous with relatively compact support U disjoint from tau(U), positive Kontsevich integral
findings.counterexample: The exact cube witness has equal perimeters 5920 before normalization and unequal boundary dart counts. An orientation-reversing element of Stab(gamma) swaps its labels, giving h(G)=1 and h(tau G)=0 on an open positive-WP-measure set. The length cutoff is unchanged. Therefore the asserted weighted measure is not invariant.
findings.core_dependency: The incorrectly claimed descent is used in the construction of the intermediate quotient measure and the coset unfolding of Proposition6.6, hence in the principal convergence proof.
findings.counterevidence: Section7.3 expressly introduces ordered oriented curves and Stab_0 and acknowledges the labeling obstruction. This supports an intended oriented formulation, not the literal earlier descent.
verified_repairs: Symmetrize each unoriented Dirac pair with weight 1/2
Count oriented curves and normalize by s_or=2s_un, using actual stabilizer indices for general multicurves
findings.limits: Exact definitions, descent/count identities and the counterexample are checked; the whole corrected global convergence theorem is not reproved.

findings.title: Lemma4.8 has no bound depending only on the input inradius and bi-Lipschitz constant
findings.claim_checked: For fixed input inradius r and e^epsilon bi-Lipschitz constant, d(f(u),u') is uniformly bounded.
assumptions_checked: Each line has both companions in the same central halfplane
Every finite target has a finite genuine central inscribed circle
Global radial angular maps are bi-Lipschitz including origin and break rays
For every prescribed epsilon>0, r0 may depend on epsilon but stays fixed independently of n
findings.counterexample: Hyperboloid normals n1=(sinh2,cosh2,0), n2=(sinh2,-cosh2,0), n3(h)=(sinh h,0,cosh h), h*=log(sinh2). Centers t(h)=atanh((sinh2-sinh h)/cosh h) escape as h decreases to h*. Choose one source h0 sufficiently close to h*, and angular maps with all slopes in [exp(-epsilon),exp(epsilon)]. They fix the source center on the south ray while the target center escapes.
findings.core_dependency: The false general center lemma is explicitly invoked to establish the uniform edge-weight comparison in Proposition4.2, which is used by the averaging proof.
findings.counterevidence: In the actual fixed-genus thick-surface application, the target inradius is independently bounded. The counterfamily lacks that additional bound and does not refute Proposition4.2.
findings.verified_repair: d(f(u),u') <= 2 max(exp(epsilon)r+delta(epsilon),r'). The diameter of the common C-neighborhood intersection is <=2C by the transversal/nonseparation argument. Thick-part compactness gives both inradii <=R and restores the full uniform edge estimate with explicit constants.
findings.limits: False general lemma and actual missing proof hypothesis are confirmed; no counterexample to the paper's main convergence theorem is claimed. Analytic small-epsilon strengthening is not misrepresented as a new numerical run.

findings.title: Lemma2.5 ratio-one short-arc asymptotic is false
locators: Lemma2.5 and explicit definition of ~, printed583 / PDF13
findings.claim_checked: Spine projection weight c is asymptotic with ratio one to log(1/a).
assumptions_checked: Compact hyperbolic pair of pants with each boundary length 2T
Canonical theta-spine projection weights exactly T
Dual seam is the shortest orthogeodesic in its class
T tends to infinity and seam length tends to zero
findings.counterexample: a_T=2 asinh(1/(2 sinh(T/2))) ~2 exp(-T/2), hence T/log(1/a_T) tends to 2.
findings.core_dependency: The checked downstream uses in Section3 and Lemma4.1 require only logarithmic lower growth and a uniform short-arc threshold.
findings.counterevidence: The actual cited Calderon-Farre published Lemma6.6 provides the sufficient inequalities; these were inspected and their exact substitutions into downstream estimates were supplied.
findings.verified_repair: Use min{log3, 2atanh(tanh(logsqrt3)/cosh(c/2))}<=a<=2pi/c. These imply c>=2log(1/a)+O(1) for small a and the corrected Lemma4.1 threshold.
findings.severity_reason: Minor follows the verified weaker downstream requirements and replacement estimates, not an automatic downgrade because repair is possible.
findings.limits: No universal corrected ratio two is asserted.

per_problem.independent_reasoning: The source uses unoriented curves and a distinctly labelled cut surface. The positive cube ribbon graph has two boundary cycles of14 and10 darts but equal perimeters5920; after normalizing, it lies in MRG_2,2(1,1) and differs from its label swap. The auxiliary independently reconstructed the directed-edge permutation. A compactly supported h on disjoint U and tau U gives densities1 and0 on an open positive-WP-measure set for a full-stabilizer element, not merely one null point. (5.1) and the6.6 unfolding require the failed descent.
per_problem.counterevidence: The later ordered/oriented Stab0 construction identifies a consistent intended formulation but does not validate the earlier literal full-stabilizer claim.
per_problem.repair_scope: Unlabelled quotient, half-weight symmetrization, or actual oriented-count normalization; only definitions/descent/count identities are certified.

per_problem.independent_reasoning: The displayed spacelike normals are pairwise ultraparallel and mutually nonseparating. For S=sinh2,h*=log S, t_h=atanh((S-sinh h)/cosh h) tends to infinity and all three distances equal h+t_h. The radial angular maps have fixed distortion bounds tending to1 as the fixed input h0 approaches h*, yet preserve the south-ray input center. Thus for every chosen epsilon>0, one fixed input inradius and an unbounded sequence of center displacements contradict D(r,epsilon). Source p.23 inspected by root shows no target-inradius hypothesis; auxiliary checked the full neighboring argument and mapping assumptions.
per_problem.counterevidence: Thick compact-surface applications have both inradii bounded; the geometric conclusion in that restricted application is not refuted.
per_problem.repair_scope: The two-inradius intersection-diameter bound and the subsequent compact-surface edge estimate are algebraically coherent. The original false unrestricted lemma remains directly used in Proposition4.2.

per_problem.independent_reasoning: For pants with all boundaries2T, perimeter equations give spine weightT. The hexagon formula gives a_T=2asinh(1/(2sinh(T/2)))~2exp(-T/2), so T/log(1/a_T)->2, not1. The report faithfully retains the source's ratio-one convention. Downstream counting uses a coarse logarithmic lower bound and short-arc cutoff, both furnished by the separately checked cited inequalities; no failed core conclusion is demonstrated.
per_problem.repair_scope: Use the sufficient coarse inequalities, not an unproved universal ratio2 replacement.
